plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch correction
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw Salmon gene-level counts for 12 human kidney samples (12000 genes x 13 columns incl. gene symbol column), 6 treated vs 6 control, with two known processing batches balanced across condition. Because batch is a fixed, balanced covariate, the correct approach is to model it as a design term rather than pre-adjusting counts (DESeq2 with design ~ batch + condition), per consensus practice for balanced known-batch designs. The plan runs: (1) sample-structure QC on a blind variance-stabilizing transform to visualize batch/condition separation before testing; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size); (3) DESeq2 Wald test on design ~ batch + condition with condition releveled so control is the reference, giving a treated-vs-control contrast; (4) apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change for the condition coefficient; (5) BH-adjusted results at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, reporting the DE gene table; (6) an edgeR quasi-likelihood fit on the same design as an orthogonal robustness check, with the overlap between DESeq2 and edgeR significant-gene calls reported as the high-confidence set; (7) over-representation enrichment of the DESeq2-significant genes against MSigDB Hallmark (or best-available functional gene sets), using the tested-gene set as the statistical universe, since no gene set store is currently provisioned in this environment and preranked GSEA is not the permitted method for this two-group standard design. Each step states version/design/threshold details for reproducibility, and package availability is probed defensively since the environment's package inventory could not be read.
